notes.meaning: Here is the central truth of the whole discussion: believers have a High Priest who has taken His seat at the right hand of God's throne in heaven. In the earthly tabernacle, priests never sat down because their sacrificial work was never finished. Jesus sat down because His work of salvation is completed and He now reigns in glory.

Jesus serves as our minister in heaven, the real and original sanctuary set up by the Lord rather than human hands. The tent Moses built in the desert was only a temporary model of this heavenly reality. In God's actual presence, Christ carries out His priestly work on our behalf.

Every high priest is appointed to present gifts and sacrifices to God, so Jesus also had to have an offering. He did not bring animal blood, but offered His own body and blood once for all on the cross. Having finished that sacrifice, He presents its lasting value before the Father in heaven.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ's heavenly priesthood continually presents His one sacrifice to the Father, and this same sacrifice is made present on earth in the celebration of the Mass.

notes.meaning: If Jesus were living on earth, He would not even be allowed to serve as a priest. The law of Moses required priests to come from the family of Aaron in the tribe of Levi, while Jesus came from the tribe of Judah. Because earthly worship already had its appointed priests, Christ's priesthood must be exercised in heaven.

The Levitical priests served in an earthly tent that was merely a shadow and copy of heavenly things. God gave Moses strict instructions to build the tabernacle according to the exact blueprint revealed to him on Mount Sinai. That earthly structure was never meant to be the final reality, but only an outline pointing forward to Christ.

Jesus has been given a priestly ministry far superior to the work of earthly priests. He is the mediator—the one who bridges the gap between God and humanity—of a vastly better covenant, or sacred agreement. This new arrangement is better because it is built on greater promises of inner transformation and eternal life.

If the first covenant made at Mount Sinai had been completely sufficient to save people, God would never have needed to replace it. The law itself was holy and good, but it could not provide lasting forgiveness or conquer human weakness. Because it could not bring full salvation, God prepared the way for a second covenant.

God showed the limits of the old arrangement by pointing out the unfaithfulness of the people who lived under it. Through the prophet Jeremiah, the Lord promised that a time would come when He would make a new covenant with Israel and Judah. This prophecy proved long ago that the old system was never intended to last forever.

differ.view: The promise to Israel and Judah is fulfilled in the Christian church, where believing Jews and Gentiles together form the one people of God.
The new covenant belongs primarily to national Israel and Judah, and its ultimate fulfillment will happen during a future earthly kingdom.

notes.meaning: This new covenant would be very different from the one made when God led Israel out of Egypt like a loving parent guiding a child by the hand. Despite that tender care, the people repeatedly broke God's laws and wandered away. Because they broke faith with Him, God turned away from them and allowed them to suffer the consequences of their disobedience.

Instead of carving His commandments on stone tablets, God promises to place His laws inside the minds and hearts of His people. The Holy Spirit renews believers from within, giving them both the understanding and the genuine desire to obey Him. In this close relationship, God pledges Himself to be their God, and they become His devoted people.

Under the new covenant, every believer enjoys a direct and personal relationship with God. People no longer depend entirely on human teachers or priests to introduce them to the Lord, because the Holy Spirit teaches them inwardly. From the least important person to the most prominent, all of God's people have access to this saving knowledge.

All the blessings of the new covenant rest upon God's promise of complete pardon. Through the sacrifice of Christ, God shows mercy toward human wrongdoing and promises never to hold past sins against believers again. This total forgiveness brings true peace of mind and frees people to serve God with gladness.

By speaking of a new covenant, God declared that the first one given at Sinai had grown old and outdated. In everyday life, whatever becomes old and worn out is close to disappearing completely. When the temple in Jerusalem was destroyed shortly after this letter was written, the earthly sacrificial rituals vanished just as Scripture anticipated.
